title: Extract android_guardian and settle the heavy_job_lock seam
objective: Move the Magisk module to its own public repo. The directory it lived in also held heavy_job_lock.sh, a shared lock library that is NOT part of the module, so this extraction has to split the directory rather than move it wholesale. It also inherits a packaging script whose module path was already broken before the extraction.
acceptance_criteria: The module and both its test suites are in the new public repo, tests passing from a clean clone, shellcheck exiting 0 with no severity filter.
heavy_job_lock.sh lands where its installer is, justified by measuring which consumers read the repo copy versus the installed /usr/local/bin copy - not by the ad-hoc '>2 consumers' rule.
install_pacman_wrapper.sh's relative path to heavy_job_lock.sh resolves after the move.
update_android_hosts.sh points at a real location, and a missing checkout fails with an actionable message at a single funnel rather than a bare cp error deep in a helper.
The module still builds end-to-end from the new checkout.
shell-tests.yml names no removed suite; the coverage allowlist names no removed path.
periodic_background/utils/ is fully emptied, not left as a one-file directory.
out_of_scope: Moving heavy_job_lock.sh to ~/utils: the measurement does not support it, and every consumer but the installer already reads the installed copy.
The adb push half of update_android_hosts.sh, which needs a device in a writable state.
digital_wellbeing itself, which is the next and last extraction.
verifier: bash tests/*.sh in the new repo passes; shellcheck exits 0 there; ANDROID_GUARDIAN_DIR=/nonexistent produces the guard message; a real run builds the zip (182331 domains); shellcheck and check_shell_coverage.sh --all clean here; check_directory_depth.sh --all continues to fall.
